bodyHtml:
A decision guide to Tailwind CSS: what it is for, when it fits, how to start, and which compatibility or maintenance details deserve a closer look.

Quick verdict

A utility-first CSS framework for rapidly building custom user interfaces.

Shortlist Tailwind CSS only if its documented purpose matches your use case; the source signals below are context, not an endorsement.

Best fit — and when to skip it

Tailwind CSS is most relevant to developers working with JavaScript/TypeScript. It belongs on a shortlist when that stated purpose matches a concrete requirement.

Skip or postpone it when the documented runtime, license, dependency footprint, or maintenance model conflicts with your project. Popularity alone is not a reason to migrate.

Setup and first checks

Confirm the exact package name, current version, runtime requirement, dependencies, provenance, and release notes before installing tailwindcss in a production project. Start in a disposable example and exercise the use case you actually need.

Maintenance and risk signals

The collected source record shows 114.1M weekly downloads, version 4.3.3, and released 2026-07-16.

The registry lists 3 maintainers.

The source reports the MIT license.

Registry downloads include automated requests and are not unique users, satisfaction, or proof of quality.

Bottom line

Tailwind CSS is worth a closer look when its stated purpose and ecosystem fit your project. Compare it with related tools, verify the current documentation, and test the smallest realistic use case before committing.

Try it safely

npm install tailwindcss

Use the official npm package page to confirm the current version, documentation, dependencies, provenance, and compatibility requirements before installing it in an important project.
